Reviewer misread the hardware generation. Qwen claims H100 delivers the same FLOP/s in FP16 and FP8; on H100 SXM the FP8 Tensor Core dense peak is 1,979 TFLOPS against 989.5 TFLOPS dense BF16/FP16 — exactly 2x (datasheet lists 3,958 with sparsity). The book's own Ch 8 L257 states the same: 'H200's ~412 FLOP/byte ridge in *dense* FP8 - ~1.98 PFLOPS ... never the sparsity-inclusive ~4 PFLOPS'. So the L176 claim 'it lowers the bytes transferred/stored and can raise the *effective* accelerator throughput (8-bit tensor cores run at a higher peak rate)' is accurate, and it already scopes the gain to 'effective' peak rather than asserting a measured throughput doubling. Ch2 is also internally consistent with L145 ('a lower-precision path with a higher tensor-core peak (FP8 on H100...)') and L190. Applying the suggested rewrite would introduce a false claim (equal FP16/FP8 peak), so no edit applied.
